standard.title: Organisation of ideas to achieve purpose
standard.description: analyse and evaluate how authors organise ideas in texts to achieve a purpose
standard.prior_knowledge: Students analyse idea organisation in paragraphs and extended texts (AC9E9LY04). They have not yet analysed and evaluated how authors organise ideas in texts to achieve a specific purpose.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse and evaluate how authors organise ideas in texts to achieve a purpose.

nodes.label: Analysing organisation of ideas
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse how ideas are organised in a text and explain the purpose and effect of the organisational choices.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify how ideas are organised in a text and explain the purpose of that organisation.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how the organisation of ideas in a range of texts — print, digital and multimodal — achieves different purposes, examining how structure guides the reader's attention and understanding.
wider: Compare how ideas are organised in texts designed for different platforms (print versus web page) and analyse how the platform shapes organisational choices
Examine how the organisation of ideas in political pamphlets or advocacy texts achieves persuasive purposes
Analyse how First Nations Australian authors organise ideas in ways that reflect non-linear or culturally specific narrative or argumentative structures
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires students to evaluate the effectiveness of idea organisation — a judgement that depends on first being able to identify and explain the organisational structure and its intended purpose. Without this, evaluation has no object.

response_modes.reason: Organisational patterns vary substantially across print, digital and multimodal texts — students who have only analysed one text type may not recognise how purpose shapes organisation in other formats; breadth across text types builds reliable identification.

success_criteria: Identifies how ideas are organised in a text
Explains the purpose the organisational structure serves for the audience

nodes.label: Evaluating effectiveness of organisation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate how the organisation of ideas in a text achieves its purpose, making supported judgements.
nodes.minimum_width: Make a supported judgement about whether the organisation of ideas in a text is effective in achieving its purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate the effectiveness of idea organisation across a range of texts and purposes, comparing how different organisational strategies succeed or fail in achieving their intended purposes.
wider: Compare the organisation of ideas in two online reviews of the same product or text and evaluate which achieves its purpose more effectively and why
Evaluate how the organisation of ideas in a political pamphlet shapes reader response, assessing whether the structure achieves the intended persuasive effect
Evaluate how ideas organised in a non-linear structure (e.g. a web page with navigation, or a non-linear narrative) achieve effects not possible through linear organisation

response_modes.reason: Effectiveness of organisation is purpose- and platform-dependent — what works on a webpage may not work in print; students need contrasting contexts to evaluate organisation in relation to purpose rather than applying a single standard.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Comparative evaluation across digital, print and political texts offers rich work — the contrast between linear and non-linear organisation, and between different persuasive purposes, provides substantial analytic depth.
success_criteria: Makes a supported judgement about the effectiveness of a text's organisational structure
Connects the evaluation to the text's specific purpose and intended audience
